clue.text: Dawn sees one bird leaving another

indicators.note: one bird leaving another means the first bird's letters depart from the longer word for dawn

parts.note: cockcrow is the time the rooster calls, so daybreak
a crow is a common black bird

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher at daybreak sees one bird fly off from another.
explanation.walkthrough: Take CROW out of COCKCROW (dawn) and the other bird is left.
explanation.definitionFit: A rooster is itself a bird, so it is the second bird the clue mentions.

clue.text: Start to caper, jump about, and dance quickly

indicators.note: start to means the first letter of the following word

parts.note: to hop is to jump
C abbreviates circa, about
a hop is an informal dance

explanation.surface: A dancer is told to caper and leap around, moving at speed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like part of 'jump about' but gives C.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an informal urging to hurry up, meaning quickly.

clue.text: Some wear at the top, given tight fit round base of nut

definitions.text: Some wear at the top, given tight fit round base of nut

parts.words: Some wear at the top, given tight fit round base of nut
parts.note: clothing worn on top with a close collar round the bottom of the nut, slang for head, so round the neck

explanation.definitionFit: A sweater with a close-fitting round collar is named after this neckline sitting at the base of the neck.

clue.text: Horrid things that may be said when lying

definitions.text: that may be said when lying

indicators.note: horrid suggests something messed up and ugly, signalling the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the plural is read as two lots of the word thing, each to be scrambled

explanation.surface: Nasty remarks someone might make while telling lies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lying' looks like telling untruths, but it means lying in bed. 'Things' supplies two THINGs, and 'Horrid' rearranges each into NIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: A goodnight farewell, spoken to someone lying down to sleep, is a childlike pair of repeated words.

clue.text: One very dry part of France

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
sere means withered and parched

explanation.surface: One region of France is extremely arid.
explanation.definitionFit: A French department and river in the Alps share this name, so it is a part of France.

clue.text: Help firm that's very ill-advised without one

parts.note: a house is a business firm, as in a publishing house

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the word for one sits inside

parts.note: mad means wildly unwise
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Assistance from a company acting foolishly without anyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Help' is a noun, the domestic help; 'without' carries its old sense of outside, so the piece for one sits within.
explanation.definitionFit: Domestic servants are called the help, and a female servant cleaning a home is one.

clue.text: The setting of standards on rationalism is ordered

indicators.note: ordered means put into order, signalling these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Standards are set when rationalism is brought into order.
explanation.definitionFit: Bringing things to conform to a norm is the process of setting standards.

clue.text: Insincerely introduce bishop to grand woman

parts.note: G is slang for a grand, a thousand

indicators.note: introduce means insert, so the bishop goes inside the woman's name

parts.note: Lily is a woman's name
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A guest is told to present a bishop to a grand lady without meaning it.
explanation.definitionFit: Speaking smoothly but shallowly, without real feeling, is speaking insincerely.

clue.text: Fly from longest-established rising

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the letters read from bottom to top
from tells us the letters are taken out of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A fly comes from the oldest established stock.
explanation.walkthrough: ESTEST sits inside 'longest-established'; 'rising' turns it upward.
explanation.definitionFit: The African insect that spreads sleeping sickness is a biting fly.

clue.text: Manage to set poetry into old English

indicators.note: set into tells us the poetry is placed inside the abbreviation for old English

parts.note: verse is another word for poetry

explanation.surface: A task: arrange for poetry to be rendered in Old English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set' merely supports the insertion signalled by 'into'; 'to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To oversee a project is to supervise or manage it.

clue.text: Zoom lens seeks out where fogging is less likely to occur

definitions.text: where fogging is less likely to occur

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A photographer's zoom lens looks for places where pictures will not fog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fogging' suggests misty camera images, but means smog, which British clean-air areas reduced.
explanation.definitionFit: British towns designated areas where burning coal was banned to cut smog, so fog is less frequent there.

clue.text: Britain's weather heading east — eventually here?

parts.note: UK is the abbreviation for the United Kingdom, Britain
rain is typical British weather
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: British rain drifting eastward may end up somewhere far off.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the playful idea that weather moving east from Britain eventually reaches this country.
explanation.definitionFit: Weather travelling east across Europe from Britain would in time arrive at this large eastern European country.

clue.text: Colours on tin ultimately indicate a way to cook

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece on another means it follows it

parts.note: a can is a tin
tones are shades or colours

indicators.note: ultimately means the final letter of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: Paint colours on a tin show a method of cooking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' in an across clue means coming after, so the colours follow the tin; 'ultimately' takes the last letter of 'indicate'.
explanation.definitionFit: Chinese cooking from the Canton region is a recognised cuisine, so it names a style of preparing food.

clue.text: A wit rejected God

indicators.note: rejected suggests being thrown back, so the word for wit is read backwards

parts.note: salt means sharp wit, as in Attic salt

explanation.surface: A clever joker turned away by a deity.
explanation.walkthrough: Attic salt is an old phrase for refined wit; 'rejected' sends that word backwards after A.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the Titan who holds up the heavens is a god of that name.

clue.text: After jogging, their captors wind down in one

indicators.note: jogging shakes things up, so after it the letters of the next words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Escaped prisoners report their guards winding down after a run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wind' is not to relax: it means wind instruments, played down below the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: The sunken area in front of a stage holds the musicians, including the wind players, below stage level.

clue.text: Union's present artist has a little time over

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means placed above, so it comes first

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
Henri Rousseau was a French painter

explanation.surface: A painter has a little time left over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Union' is a marriage, so its present is what the bride brings.
explanation.definitionFit: A bride's collection of clothes and linen for married life is her contribution to the marriage union.

clue.text: Do we have an arrangement for five? It's on the cards

definitions.text: Do we have an arrangement for five? It's on the cards

parts.words: Do we have an arrangement for five? It's on the cards
parts.note: the five pips on a playing card form a pattern of four corners and a centre

explanation.definitionFit: Five points arranged as four corners and a centre, as on dice or playing cards, form this pattern.

clue.text: Agreed to be told by judge

parts.note: to hear is to be told something
a judge hears a case in court

explanation.surface: A judge confirms what is agreed.
explanation.definitionFit: In Parliament the doubled cry expresses agreement with a speaker.

clue.text: Habit about to be exhumed from unconsecrated ground

indicators.note: ground means crushed and remade, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: C stands for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: A churchyard habit: digging up the dead from unholy soil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To be exhumed from' tells us C (about) is removed from UNCONSECRATED; 'ground' anagrams what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: A habit so ingrained that it feels instinctive is said to be one's natural way of behaving.

clue.text: Chain unevenly joined to itself in dance

indicators.note: joined to itself means the letters are repeated
unevenly picks the odd-numbered letters of the next word

explanation.surface: A chain of dancers links up in a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A high-kicking French music-hall routine is a lively dance.

clue.text: Girl finally dropped boy, and did this?

indicators.note: the girl's name loses its final letter

parts.note: Jill is a girl's name
Ted is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A girl dumped her boyfriend in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition refers back to the wordplay's own story: she dropped the boy, so she did this.
explanation.definitionFit: Dropping a boyfriend abruptly is exactly what a girl who did this has done.

clue.text: House break-ins down by half

indicators.note: reduced by half means the first five of ten letters are removed

parts.note: burglaries are break-ins

explanation.surface: Burglaries at homes have fallen fifty per cent.
explanation.walkthrough: BURGLARIES loses its first half, BURGL. 'House' is an astrological house, one of the twelve divisions of the zodiac.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ram is the first sign of the zodiac, and astrologers call each sign a house.

clue.text: I supply rulers with imperial pads perhaps

definitions.text: I supply rulers with imperial pads perhaps

parts.words: I supply rulers with imperial pads perhaps
parts.note: rulers sound like monarchs and imperial pads like palaces, but they are measuring sticks and notepads sold in a shop

explanation.definitionFit: A shopkeeper selling paper, pens and rulers deals in writing materials.

clue.text: A maxim shortly taken up with others

indicators.note: in a down clue, taken up means the letters read upwards
shortly means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a gnome is a pithy saying, a maxim

explanation.surface: A short saying taken up together with other people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shortly' removes the final E; 'taken up' then reads the rest upwards, as this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in the midst of a group means being with others.

clue.text: Where you'd currently finish being positive

definitions.text: Where you'd currently finish being positive

parts.words: Where you'd currently finish being positive
parts.note: currently means as an electric current: where conventional current ends up, an electrode that is positive inside a battery

explanation.definitionFit: This electrode is where conventional current leaves a device, and in a battery it is the positive terminal.

clue.text: Regularly goofier, without common sense?

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the alternate letters surround the next piece
regularly picks every other letter of the following word

parts.note: nous is British slang for common sense

explanation.surface: Someone getting sillier by the day, lacking any practical sense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' takes the 2nd, 4th and 6th letters of 'goofier'; 'without' means outside. The whole clue also describes uselessness.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone lacking common sense, and goofier all the time, is useless.

clue.text: Get prompt on more than one occasion, but say no more

definitions.text: Get prompt on more than one occasion
definitions.meaning: a nudge is a prompt, so two of them are repeated prompting
the knowing catchphrase from a Monty Python sketch, a wink of innuendo

explanation.definitionFit: A double poke is repeated prompting, and the Monty Python phrase accompanies a knowing say-no-more wink.

clue.text: Fence in dogs, cutting off either side

indicators.note: removing a letter from each side means the first and last letters go

parts.note: boxers are a breed of dog

explanation.surface: Dogs are kept penned in, with the sides of the enclosure removed.
explanation.walkthrough: BOXERS loses its first and last letters. 'In' is a link word, not a container.
explanation.definitionFit: In show jumping, a spread fence with rails is called by this name.
